findings.title: Count and fetch can observe different database snapshots
findings.description: The count is used to enforce the response-row ceiling, but the subsequent fetch runs as a separate statement under the pool’s default `READ COMMITTED` isolation. A concurrent insert committed between those statements can be included in the fetch without being included in the count, so the endpoint may return more than `max_rows` (the same pattern appears in the trades route at lines 160-163). Use a consistent snapshot for the count and fetch, or otherwise re-check the limit before returning rows.

findings.title: Trade watermark is documented as the newest stored trade
findings.description: The `tape_complete_through` description says it is the created time of the newest stored trade. The route actually supplies the persisted sync watermark, which represents how far collection is complete and can be later than the last trade. This description is exposed in the API schema and can lead clients to treat a coverage timestamp as trade activity.

findings.title: Filtered status incorrectly promises that no trades are stored
findings.description: The description says `tape_filtered: true` means no trades are stored for the market. The collection filter prevents matching trades from being stored on the write path, but does not remove trades stored before the filter was applied. Thus a filtered market can still return historical trades. Describe this as a collection-policy status, not a guarantee that the tape is empty.
